title: Anchor-preserving recent-pool isolated qualification
benchmark: A frozen learned policy plays at least 100,000 fresh 200bb HUNL Slumbot hands, scores above 0 bb/100, and has a 95% confidence-interval lower bound above 0.
hypothesis: Keeping external anchors while admitting recent learned snapshots removes observed near-static historical-loss selection; strength remains untested.
material_change: Isolated opt-in selection component and actual retained-parent pool fixtures; no trainer defaults or existing checkpoints changed.
notes: Both exact retained connected2M pool fixtures preserve initial slot order and pool tensors; three synthetic candidates replace only learned slots and roundtrip retains monotonic IDs. Synthetic payloads are not poker policies or training checkpoints. Full trainer resume/optimizer/replay/EMA reconciliation not qualified by this component test.

result.summary: Implemented isolated anchor-latest selector; both actual connected2M parent-pool fixtures and five edge cases passed without new poker.
result.conclusion: Recency admission and anchor preservation work at component level, including load order and monotonic snapshot IDs. No evidence of poker-strength improvement and no full trainer integration claim.
result.decision: Proceed to isolated trainer integration and exact retained-state resume qualification before allocating training. Leave production defaults and historical evidence unchanged.
result.next_step: Add explicit opt-in strategy to candidate trainer, verify restored model/optimizer/replay/pool and adaptive slot reconciliation on the two retained parents, then preregister matched geometric learned-weight training against loss-kbest.
